title: Creator In Residence (Instagram)
description:
About HeyGen
At HeyGen, our mission is to make visual storytelling accessible to all. Over the last decade, visual content has become the preferred method of information creation, consumption, and retention. But the ability to create such content, in particular videos, continues to be costly and challenging to scale. Our ambition is to build technology that equips more people with the power to reach, captivate, and inspire audiences.
Learn more at www.heygen.com. Visit our Mission and Culture doc here.
About the role
HeyGen is hiring a Creator in Residence to own short-form Instagram content and bring consumer-grade viral instinct to the team. The job is to create content yourself, on camera and behind it, shape the overall direction and review of our Instagram series, and hold the taste bar.
HeyGen makes it possible for anyone to produce studio-quality video with AI avatars, in any language, without a camera. Millions of people have made videos with it, and the product moves fast: new avatar models, new formats, new ways to be on screen ship constantly. What we have not yet built is a feed presence that makes people stop scrolling.
In a way, you are the creative director for short-form videos on Instagram. You are not a producer taking briefs, and you are not behind the camera only: you are on it too, as a recurring face of HeyGen's Instagram, and as the human the avatars play off. You are the single DRI for Instagram short-form, and you are measured on whether the content hits.
What you'll do
Own Instagram short-form end to end. You are the DRI for reels: what we make, how often, what it looks like, and whether it worked. Set the editorial calendar, the formats, and the bar.
Bring viral sensibility to the team. Dissect what is spreading on Instagram each week: formats, sounds, pacing, hooks. Turn that into formats we can run, and teach the team to see what you see.
Be on camera. You are one of the faces of HeyGen's Instagram. Film yourself, host formats, react, riff, and put your own personality in the feed. Your avatar will be in the daily series too.
Direct talent, human and avatar. Coach founders, teammates and creators on camera. Write and direct for avatars so they read as a character, not a demo.
Experiment on a schedule. Ship a new format every week, read the numbers, keep what hits, cut what does not.
Make the final creative call. Approve or kill every piece before it ships. When the team disagrees, you decide. Taste is your job, and you are accountable for it.
Report on performance. Own reach, shares, saves and follower growth on Instagram. Know why a post worked and say so.
Who you are
You have made things go viral, repeatedly. A portfolio of short-form videos with real reach, on your own account or a brand's. One hit is luck; we want a pattern.
You have consumer instincts, not B2B ones. You know what a 19-year-old shares with a friend at midnight. You have built an audience of 50k+ on Instagram, TikTok or YouTube, or run an account that did.
You have taste, and you can defend it. You can say why a cut is wrong in one sentence. You hold a bar and other people can feel it.
You are comfortable being the decider. You have led a team or a crew and made calls that other people executed. You do not need to touch every frame to own the result.
You live in the feed. You know this week's sounds, formats and hooks before they peak, and you can tell a trend from a fad.
You are good on camera and you can direct. On-camera talent, founders, and avatars. You write for performance and know how to get a take.
You edit well enough to fix the last 5% yourself. CapCut, Premiere or similar. You do not need to be the fastest editor on the team, but you need to see what the editor missed.
You read numbers without flinching. Reach, shares, saves, retention curves. You change what you make based on what they say.
3+ years making short-form content for social, with at least some of it in a brand or team setting.
Bonus points
You have made AI-generated or avatar-led content that people did not scroll past
You have built a recurring series or character that an audience came back for
You have grown a brand account from zero in a crowded category
You have created for a startup, a tech product, or the creator economy
How this role works
We run creative on a 15/80/5 model, and this role sits at both ends of it.
Phase
Share of the work
Who
What happens
Concept
First 15%
You, deep in it
Hook, premise, format, casting, the reason anyone would watch
Production
Middle 80%
Team executes
Shooting, avatar generation, editing, captions, scheduling
Final call
Last 5%
You, back in it
Review every cut, fix what is close, kill what is not, approve what ships
You are the DRI for Instagram short-form. That means one name on the result, not a committee. You will work closely with brand, product marketing and the avatar team, and you will have editors and producers to execute. The creative call is yours.
What success looks like in the first 90 days
The avatar daily series is live, consistent and growing week over week
Instagram reach and shares are up measurably from the day you started
At least one format has clearly broken out and become a repeatable franchise
The team can name the three things you changed about how we judge creative
Why HeyGen
The most interesting tool a creator has ever had. You will make content with avatars, voices and formats that did not exist a year ago, and you will have the people who build them down the hall.
Real creative authority. You make the call. No creative review by committee, no six-week approval chain.
A product people already love. You are not inventing demand. You are showing millions of people what is possible in a way they cannot ignore.
A team that ships. We move at the speed of the feed and we expect you to pull us faster.
Competitive salary, equity, health coverage, and the equipment you need. Hybrid in San Francisco or Los Angeles.
HeyGen considers factors such as scope and responsibilities of the position, candidate's work experience, education/training, key skills, as well as location, market and business considerations when extending an offer.
HeyGen is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.
Join us at HeyGen and be part of a team that's making visual storytelling accessible to all!

description:

About HeyGen
At HeyGen, our mission is to make visual storytelling accessible to all. Over the last decade, visual content has become the preferred method of information creation, consumption, and retention. But the ability to create such content, in particular videos, continues to be costly and challenging to scale. Our ambition is to build technology that equips more people with the power to reach, captivate, and inspire audiences. Learn more at www.heygen.com. Visit our Mission and Culture doc here.
The Role
We are hiring Sales Development Representatives to build the pipeline behind HeyGen's next phase of growth. This is a full-funnel prospecting role with a heavy emphasis on outbound. You will research target accounts, run creative outbound campaigns, work product-led signals, qualify interest, and book first meetings for our Account Executives. This is not a traditional SDR role where you work someone else's list and a fixed script. We are looking for hunters who are comfortable moving fast, testing new outbound ideas, starting conversations with busy buyers, and earning meetings through persistence, creativity, and sharp research. You will prospect into companies using HeyGen's web app and API, helping buyers see how AI video can transform marketing, sales enablement, customer education, training, localization, product onboarding, and developer-powered video workflows.
What You'll Do
Build pipeline from scratch - You will run high-volume, high-quality outbound into target accounts. This includes cold email, phone, LinkedIn, personalized video, account research, trigger-based outreach, and creative campaign ideas. You should be excited by the idea of starting conversations that would not have happened without you.
Mine product-led signals - You will work with self-serve users, product usage data, sign-ups, and inbound interest to find the teams already getting value from HeyGen who are ready for a bigger conversation.
Qualify with discipline - You will run first conversations that uncover real pain, identify who owns the budget, and understand timing, so every meeting you book is one an Account Executive wants to take.
Sell the outcome, not just the meeting - You will help prospects see how HeyGen can reduce video production costs, speed up content creation, improve localization, personalize customer communication, and unlock new video workflows, so they show up to the first call already curious.
Move fast and test - You will try new messaging, channels, personas, and sequences, measure what works, and share it with the team. Most experiments fail; the ones that work become the playbook.
Partner with Account Executives - You will align with AEs on target accounts, share what you are hearing in the market, and hand off the context they need to run a strong first meeting.
Maintain strong pipeline discipline - You will keep CRM data clean, log activity accurately, and understand the difference between a real opportunity and a polite maybe.
What We're Looking For
1+ years of experience in sales, business development, or another target-driven role.
A track record of meeting or exceeding activity, meeting, or pipeline targets.
Experience generating pipeline through outbound prospecting across email, phone, and LinkedIn.
Strong discovery instincts and the ability to find a real business problem in a first conversation.
Comfort reaching out to marketing, sales, customer success, L&D, product, operations, founder, or technical stakeholders.
A high-agency, builder mindset. You do not wait for perfect playbooks. You test, learn, and iterate.
Strong written communication skills. Your cold emails and follow-ups should be clear, short, and get replies.
Curiosity about AI, video, creative workflows, and API-driven products.
Nice-to-Haves
SDR or BDR experience at a PLG, usage-based, API, creative software, marketing technology, sales technology, or AI company.
Experience prospecting into marketing, localization, customer education, learning and development, sales enablement, ecommerce, media, or product teams.
Experience using video, personalization, AI tools, or creative outbound to start conversations.
Experience working in an early-stage or high-growth startup environment.
Who Will Thrive Here
Gets energy from prospecting and hunting.
Can write a sharp cold email without waiting for marketing to give you a template.
Is comfortable making calls, sending videos, testing messaging, and following up persistently.
Treats a target as a game to win, not a burden.
Does not need a fully built sales playbook to be productive.
Wants to become a top-performing Account Executive and is willing to earn it.
Is competitive, resourceful, and organized.
Knows how to balance volume with thoughtful qualification.
Compensation & Benefits
Competitive base salary plus variable pay.
Equity in a high-growth AI company.
Health, dental, and vision benefits.
Flexible PTO.
A clear path into a closing Account Executive role.
High ownership, high velocity, and direct impact on revenue growth.
Equal Opportunity HeyGen is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We value diversity and are committed to building an inclusive environment for all employees.

title: Community Manager, US East
description:
About HeyGen
At HeyGen, our mission is to make visual storytelling accessible to all. Over the last decade, visual content has become the preferred method of information creation, consumption, and retention. But the ability to create such content, in particular videos, continues to be costly and challenging to scale. Our ambition is to build technology that equips more people with the power to reach, captivate, and inspire audiences.
Learn more at www.heygen.com. Visit our Mission and Culture doc here.
The Role
We are hiring a Community Manager to build and grow HeyGen's in-person community across the US East region. This is a long-term, part-time contract (15-25 hours per week) with frequent travel. You will lead workshops for creators and small businesses, run HeyGen's presence at tradeshows and conferences, and recruit and activate local ambassadors and partners. This is an independent, builder role. You will own the region end to end: set the plan, open doors, and do the hands-on work yourself, whether that is leading a room of small business owners, staffing a booth, or coaching an ambassador through their first event. Within 12 months, success looks like US tradeshows that run smoothly, on time, and on budget, an active group of ambassadors and partners hosting their own events, a regular cadence of workshops across key East Coast cities, and measurable pipeline and user activation coming out of all of it. Over time, you will build a community engine that grows beyond what you can run alone.
What You'll Do
Lead hands-on workshops and meetups - You will run HeyGen workshops and meetups for creators, partners' audiences, and small businesses, co-host events with partners, and support ambassador-led events. You will keep content current as HeyGen ships and follow up with attendees to drive activation.
Own tradeshow and conference logistics - You will manage assigned tradeshows and conferences end to end, from booth registration and shipping to vendors, staffing, and teardown. Tradeshow support may span the entire US, not only the East Coast.
Staff the booth - You will run demos, capture leads, and route attendees to the right team.
Organize side events - You will plan dinners, happy hours, and pop-up workshops around major events, and report on results.
Build and run the regional community plan - You will set a community plan for the US East region that aligns with HeyGen's global direction.
Recruit and activate ambassadors - You will find, enable, and support local ambassadors who educate users, host events, and represent HeyGen.
Open local partnerships - You will build relationships with business associations, accelerators, agencies, and AI communities across the region.
Feed insights back to the team - You will track community activity and share what you are seeing with the global community and marketing team.
What We're Looking For
Experience as a community builder, creator, or ecosystem operator, with a track record of working independently.
Hands-on conference or tradeshow experience, such as planning logistics, staffing booths, or running activations.
Comfort leading workshops, trainings, meetups, or community gatherings, and a willingness to roll up your sleeves and build new skills.
You drive outcomes through relationships rather than headcount, and you are comfortable reaching out to new people.
Organized and proactive in outreach, follow-up, and event logistics.
Tech-savvy and curious about AI. You enjoy showing others how to use new tools.
Based near a major East Coast hub such as New York, DC, Atlanta, or Miami.
Able to travel frequently (often 25-50%), including some evenings and weekends, and to transport event materials.
Nice-to-Haves
Experience working with partners to co-host events, workshops, or conference activations.
Experience as a trainer or teacher.
Experience working with creators, small businesses, or SaaS products.
Existing relationships with East Coast business associations, accelerators, agencies, or creator networks.
Who Will Thrive Here
Wants to own a whole region, not run someone else's playbook.
Is as comfortable leading a room of small business owners as breaking down a booth at the end of the day.
Gets energy from meeting new people and turning them into partners and ambassadors.
Thinks about building something that keeps growing without them in every room.
Likes a flexible schedule where event-heavy weeks trade off with prep and outreach weeks.
Logistics
Engagement: Long-term contract, part-time.
Hours: 15-25 hours per week, varying between event-heavy weeks and weeks focused on workshop prep and outreach.
Location: Remote, US East, based near a major East Coast hub such as New York, DC, Atlanta, or Miami.
Travel: Frequent travel across the US East Coast plus occasional national conferences, with expenses covered.
Be the face of HeyGen across the East Coast and shape how creators and businesses adopt AI video.
Real ownership and autonomy over a whole region.
Work with a fast-moving, creative community and marketing team that values ambition, clarity, and curiosity.
A note on the application questions: please answer concisely and in your own words. Applications with long AI-written answers lacking substance will not be reviewed.
Equal Opportunity

title: Product Marketing MBA Intern (Contract)
description:
About HeyGen
At HeyGen, our mission is to make visual storytelling accessible to all. Over the last decade, visual content has become the preferred method of information creation, consumption, and retention. But the ability to create such content, in particular videos, continues to be costly and challenging to scale. Our ambition is to build technology that equips more people with the power to reach, captivate, and inspire audiences.
Learn more at www.heygen.com. Visit our Mission and Culture doc here.
The Role
HeyGen ships fast, and every release deserves a launch that does it justice. We are looking for a product marketer to own our launches end to end: the calendar, the story, the video, the rollout, and the results. Our launches are X-led, so you will craft the strategy and story that carry each release, then brief every partner and channel, keep Product, Sales, and Marketing moving together, and measure the success. This is a hands-on, full-time, 6-month contract based in San Francisco or Los Angeles, starting January 2027, for someone who can set the strategy and also do the work. Based on performance and business needs, the contract may convert to a permanent role, which could mean leading product marketing for a specific HeyGen product line.
What You'll Do
Own launch strategy and execution - You will run the launch calendar and decide where, when, and how we announce new products. For each priority release, you will craft the story for our X-led launches, defining the audience, positioning, messaging, proof, and success metrics, and scale the rollout to the size of the release.

title: Agent Infrastructure Engineer
description:
About HeyGen
At HeyGen, our mission is to make visual storytelling accessible to all. Over the last decade, visual content has become the preferred method of information creation, consumption, and retention. But the ability to create such content, in particular videos, continues to be costly and challenging to scale. Our ambition is to build technology that equips more people with the power to reach, captivate, and inspire audiences.
Learn more at www.heygen.com. Visit our Mission and Culture doc here.
About the Agentic Video team
The Agentic Video team owns HyperFrames which is our open-source framework for turning code into video. Our agent's videos are just an HTML composition. Agents author it and humans collaborate with agents in our Studio to refine it before it renders deterministically to video. Since launching in April 2026, HyperFrames has grown to nearly 90,000 GitHub stars. More than 350,000 developers use it every week to render over 7 million videos, and most of them work through a coding agent.
Now we're building on top of it by creating the best coding agents for video and a collaborative video ecosystem for teams. These agents run in our cloud on a user's behalf as well as locally on a developer's own machine. They write and run code, generate media, and then hand their work to a cloud rendering platform that turns it into finished video at scale.
About the role
You will build and own the infrastructure that lets HyperFrames agents run safely and reliably, wherever they run. That covers:
our sandboxing platform
durable execution for long-running agent sessions
governance and security for agents in our cloud and on users' machines
HyperFrames cloud rendering
This is a senior, high-ownership role. Much of the work is greenfield, and you will set the technical direction and roadmap for agent infrastructure as well as execute on it.
You'll work closely with the engineers building our agents, the team behind the open-source framework, and our core engineering and research teams.
What you'll do
Own the sandboxing platform. Every agent session writes and runs code: HTML, JavaScript, shell commands and headless browsers. You'll design the isolation model using microVMs and kernel sandboxes (Firecracker, Kata, gVisor or similar), Linux namespaces and cgroups. You'll own network egress policy and short-lived, least-privilege credentials for every run.
Make agent execution durable. Ensure resumable execution that checkpoints model calls and tool invocations, so an agent session survives pod failures, deploys and retries without losing the user's work.
Govern agents in the cloud and on the desktop. Decide and enforce what an agent may touch: tools, files, network access and credentials. Build the permission, policy and audit layer for cloud agents and for our local agent running on users' machines.
Run code-to-video rendering at scale. Own HyperFrames cloud rendering: the fleet of headless browsers and encoders behind millions of weekly renders. Drive down cold start, render time and cost per render, and keep output deterministic.
Make every run observable. Trace each agent run end to end, from prompt through model calls, tool calls and render. Feed that data into the evaluation pipelines we use to measure quality.
Set the bar. Lead design reviews, mentor engineers, own reliability and on-call for the platform, and decide what we build versus buy.
What we're looking for
You have built and operated infrastructure that runs untrusted code at scale. For example: code-execution sandboxes, agent platforms, CI runners, serverless or function platforms, or notebook and compute backends. We want to hear about an incident you handled and what you changed afterward.
You know isolation deeply. You are fluent in containers and Kubernetes and the security boundaries around them: namespaces, cgroups, seccomp, network policy, and at least one of Firecracker, Kata, gVisor, or Sysbox. You can reason about multi-tenant risk and the blast radius of running someone else's code.
You build distributed systems that recover from failure. You have shipped durable or resumable execution, such as Temporal or a checkpointing workflow engine, and you think carefully about concurrency, race conditions, and retries.
You care about performance. You have measured and reduced cold-start time, p99 latency, or cost per job on a production system.
You operate at a senior or staff level. You have 5+ years of software engineering experience. You have led the technical design of a platform other teams depend on, and you are strong in Python or TypeScript.
You take ownership. You do not wait for a spec. You find the most important problem, fix it, and tell people what changed.
A degree in computer science or a related field is welcome but not required. Equivalent experience counts.
Nice to have
You have run a code-sandbox or agent-execution product, at a company like E2B, Modal, Daytona, Fly.io, or Cloudflare, or inside a large AI lab.
You have built tool or MCP integrations, retrieval systems, or permission layers for AI agents.
You have built tracing or evaluation pipelines for LLM systems, for example with OpenTelemetry.
You have run headless-browser or media workloads at scale (Chrome/Puppeteer, FFmpeg, GPU encoding). Cloud rendering is now part of the job.
You have built security or policy tooling that runs on developer machines. That covers the local-agent governance work.
You maintain or contribute to a widely used open-source project.
Show us something you've built
With your application, please include a short note (a few sentences is fine) about infrastructure you have built and run in production: a sandbox, a runner, a workflow engine, or an agent platform. Tell us what it did, how you knew it was working, and one failure you found and fixed. A link to code or a write-up is a bonus.
Compensation & Benefits
$225,000 – $300,000 annual base.
Equity in a high-growth AI company.
401K Match.
Health, dental, and vision benefits.
Flexible PTO.
Opportunity to help define a new category in AI video.
High ownership, high velocity, and direct impact on revenue growth.
Equal Opportunity
